about: How Filo judges brands and products in the bank. From FILO Quality Fashion Brand Research V1 (sections 01, 04, 05) and the 500 Style-Led Discovery Bank V2 (section 02), both 20 Oct 2026. This is the evidence profile stored alongside Filo's existing 0-100 score. It does not replace or change that score.
principles: Higher price, natural fibre, fabric weight, 'made in Europe' or a sustainability certification does not by itself prove durability, fair labour or humane animal treatment. Evidence must be attached to the product, factory, material or supply-chain stage it covers.
A brand never scores high just because it is expensive, looks premium, uses natural fibres or says it is sustainable.
Style fit and quality evidence are separate scores.
Product first: one good product never makes a whole brand look good, and one weak product never sinks a whole brand.
Brand self-description is a lead, not proof. Leather Working Group covers tanneries, not humane slaughter. The RealReal and other resale sites are judged listing by listing.

dimension_scale.unknown: not yet checked or not disclosed

dimensions.name: Material quality and composition
dimensions.capture: Exact fibre percentages, fibre origin where disclosed, fabric weight (GSM or oz), yarn/knit/denim construction, elastane, finishing. Natural fibre alone is not a quality guarantee.

dimensions.name: Construction and durability
dimensions.capture: Close-up seam and stitch images, seam allowance, reinforced stress points, stitch consistency, hardware, lining, pilling and abrasion tests, shrinkage guidance, colourfastness, repairability. Price is a weak proxy.

dimensions.name: Manufacturing transparency and worker rights
dimensions.capture: Named factories, country and process traceability, independent worker-rights assessments, grievance mechanisms, living-wage evidence, supplier disclosure. A code of conduct alone is not proof.

dimensions.name: Animal welfare and traceability (where relevant)
dimensions.capture: Leather and suede: species, origin, farm and processor traceability, transport and slaughter evidence, tannery practices, by-product claims. Wool, down, cashmere: mulesing policy, down standard, farm-level traceability. Not applicable to all-plant or synthetic pieces; reweight when not applicable.

dimensions.name: Repairability and circularity
dimensions.capture: Repair service, spare parts, take-back or resale programs, warranty.

style_fit.capture: Distinctive design language, founder story, original silhouettes, editorial relevance, usefulness to a female-targeted style discovery experience.

evidence_levels.Very high: Strong public evidence of product-level traceability or unusually detailed supply-chain disclosure. Still verify the SKU.
evidence_levels.High: Meaningful material, manufacturing, repair, certification or sourcing evidence; some gaps at item level.
evidence_levels.Medium-high: Potentially strong product or durability proposition, but transparency is mixed or range varies.
evidence_levels.Medium: Potentially strong product or durability proposition, but brand-wide transparency is mixed or range varies substantially.
evidence_levels.Research lead: Worth investigating for design, local production or niche expertise; not yet verified.
evidence_levels.Marketplace: Not a brand endorsement. Assess individual listings.
evidence_levels.Not yet screened: Only in the style-led list or the brand directory so far.

product_decision.pass: Meets Filo's rules with evidence attached. Can be shown by the stylist.
product_decision.conditional: Passes on what is known, with named gaps. Can be shown, with the gap stated.
product_decision.hold: A known problem or a must-check item is open. Not shown.
product_decision.insufficient_evidence: Not enough to judge. Not shown.

price_rule: Store the price exactly as displayed by the brand, in its original currency, with the product URL and date checked. Convert to CAD and USD with a dated, recorded FX rate. Keep shipping, tax and duties separate. Never present a stale price as current.
